AS: Airport service — refers to services and facilities available at an airport.
ASA: As soon as — used in aviation communications and documentation to indicate immediacy.
ASDA: Accelerate stop distance available — the runway length available for acceleration and stopping during a rejected takeoff.
ASPH: Asphalt — a paved runway or taxiway surface material.
ASSOC: Associated — indicates a relationship or connection between elements in aviation contexts.
ASV: Automatic self-verification — a system capability that automatically verifies its own status or data integrity.
ATA: Actual time of arrival — the precise time an aircraft arrives at a fix, point, or destination.
ATD: Actual time of departure — the precise time an aircraft departs from a fix, point, or origin airport.
ATFM: Air traffic flow management — a service designed to ensure an optimum flow of air traffic with minimal delays.
ATIS: Automatic terminal information service — a continuous broadcast of recorded aeronautical information at airports.
ATM: Air traffic management — the dynamic, integrated management of air traffic and airspace.
ATS: Air traffic service — a generic term for flight information, alerting, and air traffic advisory services.
ATT: Attached or attachment — indicates an appended document or physically connected component.
ATZ: Aerodrome traffic zone — airspace of defined dimensions established around an aerodrome for the protection of traffic.
AUTH: Authority or authorized — refers to permission granted or the governing body granting it.
AUW: All up weight — the total weight of an aircraft including payload, fuel, and crew.
AVG: Average — the mean value used in performance calculations and weather reporting.
AVGAS: Aviation gasoline — a high-octane fuel used in piston-engine aircraft.
AVI: Aviation — the operation of aircraft and related activities.
AWOS: Automated weather observing system — an automated system that reports real-time weather conditions at airports.
AWY: Airway — a defined corridor of controlled airspace for en route IFR traffic.
AZM: Azimuth — the angular measurement of a bearing relative to true north.
BA: Braking action — a report on the effectiveness of aircraft braking on a runway surface.
BAK: Aircraft arresting system (BAK-12/14) — equipment used to safely decelerate aircraft during an aborted takeoff or overrun.
BAL: Balance — refers to the longitudinal weight distribution of an aircraft for safe flight.
BAR: Barometric — relating to atmospheric pressure as measured by a barometer.
BARO: Barometer — an instrument that measures atmospheric pressure for altimetry and weather analysis.
BC: Back course — the rearward lobe of a localizer signal used for non-precision approaches.
BCN: Beacon — a visual or electronic navigational aid that emits a distinctive signal or light.
BDRY: Boundary — the demarcation line between different airspace classifications or geographical areas.
BFR: Before — used in aviation phraseology to indicate a preceding event or time.
BGN: Begin — used to mark the start of a procedure, route segment, or action.
BHO: Burn hole(s) — damage to aircraft surfaces caused by lightning strikes or electrical arcing.
BLDG: Building — a structure that may serve as a visual reference or hazard on an aerodrome.
BLO: Below clouds — an altitude or flight condition beneath the cloud deck.
BLSN: Blowing snow — snow lifted from the surface by wind, reducing visibility.
BLW: Below — used to indicate a lower altitude, level, or value in aviation communications.
BND: Bound — indicates a direction of flight toward a specified point or destination.
BNDRY: Boundary — the dividing line between airspace sectors, control areas, or jurisdictions.
BNK: Bank — the angle of an aircraft's lateral tilt during a turn.
BOUND: Boundary — the demarcation line between airspace classifications or geographical areas.
BPL: Burst pressure limit — the maximum internal pressure a component can withstand before failure.
BPS: Bits per second — a unit of data transmission speed used in aviation data link communications.
BRG: Bearing — the direction from one point to another, measured in degrees relative to north.
BRKG: Braking — the action or effectiveness of decelerating an aircraft on the ground.
BRS: Break — a separation or interruption, such as breaking formation or breaking out of clouds.
BRSG: Breaking — the act of separating or interrupting a flight path, formation, or signal.
BRT: Bright — describes the intensity of runway or approach lighting systems.
BRV: Bravo — the ICAO phonetic word for the letter B, used in aviation communications.
BS: Business — refers to business aviation operations or business-related flight activities.
BTL: Bottle — a portable container for oxygen, hydraulic fluid, or other aircraft consumables.
BUL: Bulletin — an official publication containing aeronautical information or safety notices.
